member.name: JingleCensus
member.para: Why the narrower floor reads a jingle's end more accurately. Measured 2026-08-08 by replaying both readings over the fourteen-book corpus's own Analyze signals, parsed out of the 2026-08-07 debug logs in L:\Temp. A chapter announcement is a short VAD segment - "Kapitel eins." runs 0.6-0.9 s - so the regions' 1.0 s merge bridges straight over it. Four marks pin this down: Raumschiff Erde's chapter 1 (mark 0:05:07.28, announcement 307.48-308.41), chapter 2 (2355.07, 2355.48-2356.32) and chapter 4 (5551.38, 5551.58-5552.25), and Die Maahks' chapter 5 (6305.40, 6305.56-6306.20) - in every one the census ends the jingle within 0.2 s of the mark, where the region-based reading ran 0.6-2.3 s past it.

How the corpus tally moves with it. Both ways on the books with music (BARDIOC 29 to 32, Das Mutantenkorps 50 to 62, Die Cyber-Brutzellen 39 to 37, Wintersmith 16 to 14), and downwards on the five books with no chapter music at all - The Forever War and I Shall Wear Midnight from 1 to 0, Mort and Paula Monti from 3 to 1.

member.name: ReachSeconds
member.para: The measured longest jingle per book. 6.5 s (Rendezvous With Rama) to 33.7 s (BARDIOC), all tighter than the blind 50 s that --max-jingle-length used to hand its callers.
The one exception. "Paula Monti" at 67.5 s, a book with a single census entry which is almost certainly a musical intro rather than a chapter jingle.
